chunks: Al-Kafi: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from Abi Basir from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic
“Who is a greater wrong-doer than him who fabricates a lie against Allah, or says, ‘It has been revealed to me,’ while nothing has been revealed to him”

He said: It was revealed about Ibn Abi Sarh, whom Uthman had appointed as governor of Egypt. He was the one whose blood was permissible (to be shed) on the day of the Conquest of Mecca for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He used to write (the revelation) for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); so when Allah Mighty and Majestic sent down “Verily, Allah is Mighty, Wise”, he would write “Verily, Allah is Knowledgeable, Wise”. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would say to him: “Leave it, for indeed Allah is Knowledgeable, Wise.” And Ibn Abi Sarh used to say to the hypocrites: “I say from my own self the like of what he (the Prophet) brings, but he does not require me to change it.” Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down about him what He sent down.

key_terms.أوحى إلي: It has been revealed to me, a claim of receiving divine revelation
key_terms.ابن أبي سرح: Ibn Abi Sarh, the specific individual identified as the subject of the verse
key_terms.افتراء: Fabrication, specifically of a lie against Allah
key_terms.عزيز حكيم: Mighty, Wise, divine attributes found in the Quranic text
key_terms.هدر دمه: His blood was permissible (to be shed), a status of being worthy of execution

ai.seo_question: Who is Ibn Abi Sarh and what is the context of the verse 'Who is a greater wrong-doer than him who fabricates a lie against Allah'?
ai.summary: This hadith provides the context of revelation (asbab al-nuzul) for the verse regarding those who fabricate lies against Allah or claim revelation without receiving it. It identifies the subject as Ibn Abi Sarh, a scribe of the Prophet who would alter divine attributes (swapping 'Mighty' for 'Knowledgeable') and claimed prophetic authority for himself, leading to the revelation of the verse.

en.ammaar-muslim: [1567/1] al-Kafi: Abu Ali al-Ash’ari from Muhammad b. Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan b. Yahya from Ibn Muskan from Abi Basir from one of them عليه السلام. He (Abi Basir) said: I asked him (i.e. the Imam) about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic:
“Who is a greater wrong-doer than him who fabricates a lie against Allah, or says, ‘It has been revealed to me,’ while nothing has been revealed to him” [6:93].

He (i.e. the Imam) said: It came down about Ibn Abi Sarh whom Uthman had made governor over Egypt while he was the one whose blood the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله  had made permissible (to be shed) on the day of the conquest of Mecca.  He used to write (the revelation) for the Messenger of Allahصلى الله عليه وآله  so if Allah Mighty and Majestic sends down “Verily Allah is Mighty, Wise” he (i.e. Ibn Abi Sarh) writes (instead) “Verily Allah is Knowledgeable, Wise” so the Messenger of Allahصلى الله عليه وآله  would say to him ‘let it be - for Allah is indeed Knowledgeable, Wise’.  Ibn Abi Sarh used to say to the hypocrites: ‘I say from my own self (i.e. of my own accord) the like of what he (i.e. the prophet) comes with but he does not require me to change it’. Then Allah Blessed and Elevated sent down about him what he sent down
